slides.heading: Find Kth Largest Value In Bst
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Binary Search Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Find Kth Largest Value In Bst, a medium binary search trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Reverse in-order traversal, stopping after k nodes.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Reverse in-order traversal, stopping after k nodes.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: A reverse in-order traversal visits values from largest to smallest, so stop at the kth.
slides.narration: A reverse in-order traversal visits values from largest to smallest, so stop at the kth.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: In-order into a list, take list[n−k] → O(n) time and space
Reverse in-order, stop at k → O(h + k)
slides.narration: The simple approach collects all values in sorted order and indexes from the end, costing linear time and space. A reverse in-order traversal visits values from largest down and stops after k, so it costs only height plus k.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 3. Stop at the kth and return its value
slides.narration: Step by step. First, traverse right, node, left. Second, count visited nodes. Third, stop at the kth and return its value.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Visit #3: 17 ← k-th largest
slides.narration: Reverse in-order visit number 3 is 17. That's the third largest, so we stop.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: The walk function returns early if the node is null or we've already seen k values. It recurses right first, then counts the current node, records it as the answer if it's the k-th, and only then goes left.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of h plus k. Space is O of h.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Stop recursion once k values are seen
slides.narration: Duplicate values count separately. Make sure recursion stops as soon as the k-th value is found.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: many queries → augment nodes with subtree sizes
Iterative reverse in-order with a stack
slides.narration: For repeated queries, store subtree sizes in each node to answer in log n.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: A reverse in-order traversal visits values from largest to smallest, so stop at the kth.
